clue.text: Fish and wine served with inclusive supplement

indicators.note: inclusive means the wine word takes the supplement word within itself

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
to supplement is to add

explanation.surface: A diner orders fish with wine, and the bill carries an inclusive service supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served with' is only a link; 'inclusive' is the signal that one word goes inside the other. Hock is a German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Event of course descriptive of Houyhnhnms

definitions.meaning: a contest run on a racecourse
in Gulliver's Travels the Houyhnhnms are a race of intelligent horses

explanation.surface: A naturally occurring event, and a description of Swift's creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Event of course' reads as 'an event, naturally', but means one held on a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of galloping animals at a track, and a whole species of equine people.

clue.text: Women's work for girl employees

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a firm's staff are its employees

explanation.surface: Work for women is offered to the girls on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: A distaff is the stick that holds wool for spinning, so it came to stand for women's work and the female side of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning stick became a symbol of domestic labour traditionally done by females.

clue.text: Member of Society not even an academician

parts.note: an odd number is one that is not even
a fellow is a member of an academy or college

explanation.surface: A society member who is not even an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a mutual-aid club.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Independent Order of Oddfellows, a fraternal benefit society.

clue.text: Recoil from excitement

definitions.meaning: a gun's backward jolt when fired
a thrill, as in 'doing it for the ...'

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks back from too much thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun jolts back when fired, and a thrill is a buzz of pleasure.

clue.text: Exalted, as was Mikado's object, totally

definitions.meaning: lofty, noble, of the highest kind
in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado the emperor sings 'My object all ...', so his object was this word 'all', that is, totally

explanation.surface: A grand claim that the Mikado's aim was entirely lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; its title song begins 'My object all sublime', so 'totally' stands for 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty and noble is the ordinary sense, and the operetta lyric gives the second, literary sense.

clue.text: This necessitates adjustment of watch spring's follower

definitions.meaning: when clocks go forward an hour in spring, watches must be reset
the season that comes after spring

explanation.surface: A watch spring must be adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch spring' reads as the coil in a watch, but 'spring' is the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight saving makes us reset clocks, and the warm season follows spring.

clue.text: Second class track event or two

parts.note: B is the grade after A, second class
a race is run on a track

explanation.surface: A second-rate athlete enters one track event or a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair, as in a brace of pheasants.

clue.text: Tidy as monks are

definitions.meaning: neat, properly arranged
monks belong to a religious order

explanation.surface: Monks are neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatly arranged, and belonging to a religious brotherhood such as the Benedictines.

clue.text: Participate in record

definitions.meaning: to take part in a race or contest
to write an item into a ledger or register

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in an attempt on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining a contest, and writing data into a book or computer.

clue.text: Brought low since getting into debt

indicators.note: getting into tells us one word goes inside the other

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'

explanation.surface: Someone is brought low because they have fallen into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting into' signals the insertion. RASED is an old spelling of razed, levelled to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze a building is to level it to the ground, a literal bringing low.

clue.text: Happen to change course

definitions.meaning: to occur or take place
a sailing ship tacks onto the other heading

explanation.surface: Something happens that makes a ship alter its heading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means occur, and in sailing it means to tack onto a new heading.

clue.text: Style embraced by the Spanish for covering canines

indicators.note: embraced by means the style word sits inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
to style someone is to name or call them

explanation.surface: A Spanish fashion embraces a coat for dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embraced by' signals the insertion. 'Canines' looks like dogs but means the pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard glossy layer on teeth, including the pointed canine teeth.

clue.text: Horatius could be back

definitions.meaning: the Roman hero Horatius held the bridge against the Etruscans
in football a back is a player whose job is to guard the goal

explanation.surface: A hint that the hero Horatius might return.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatius Cocles held a bridge over the Tiber against an invading army; in football or hockey a back is a player in the rear line.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatius protected Rome at the bridge, and a back protects his side's goal.

clue.text: Relation supported by worker engaged in finance

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top, held up by the piece below

parts.note: an account is a narrative or relation of events
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A relative backed by a worker in the finance trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative, but means a telling or story.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who keeps and audits financial books for clients.

clue.text: Legitimate student expelled with dire result

indicators.note: expelled means the student is thrown out of the legal word

parts.note: legitimate means lawful, permitted by law
L stands for learner, a student driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A legitimate student is expelled, with dreadful consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expelled' removes L (learner) from LAWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire and terrible are synonyms describing something very bad.

clue.text: Competent to take in a river vessel

indicators.note: to take in means the competence word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: if you can do something you are competent to
the Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A capable crew sets out to take a boat along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To take in' signals the insertion of A plus the river. The Tamar is a river in south-west England dividing Devon from Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls, a kind of sailing craft.

clue.text: Beggar will make something good out of tin

definitions.meaning: one who lives by begging alms

definitions.text: will make something good out of tin
definitions.meaning: a tinker who mends tin cans, the word read as MEND I CAN

explanation.surface: A beggar who will make something worthwhile from scrap tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the word sounding like 'mend I can', what a tinker does with a tin can.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant friar lived by begging alms, and the tinker read is a playful sense.

clue.text: Poor men turn it into foodstuff

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Poor men turn something into food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges MEN TURN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishing matter, the sustenance taken as food.

clue.text: Joint study perhaps indicates scope for expansion

parts.note: the elbow is the joint of the arm
a study is an example of a room in a house

explanation.surface: A study of a joint shows there is space to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Space to move freely, enough room to spread one's arms.

clue.text: Fliers subscribe to a follower of hounds

indicators.note: to subscribe is literally to write below, so the birds sit under the letter in this down entry

parts.note: the letter after A in the alphabet
eagles are large flying birds of prey

explanation.surface: Airmen sign up to follow the hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A follower' is the letter that follows A in the alphabet. 'Of' is a link, and 'follower of hounds' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are small hunting dogs used for hare hunting.

clue.text: Close to the beginning of the darkness

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of the word just before

explanation.surface: Something near the start of the dark hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' takes the first letter of 'the' after NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours between sunset and sunrise.

clue.text: Catch sight of proceeds irregularly taken in notes

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is held inside the musical notes

parts.note: G and E are musical notes
to limp is to walk unevenly

explanation.surface: A glimpse of money from sales carelessly entered in notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like takings, but is the verb, goes. 'Taken in' puts LIMPS inside G and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to see briefly, a fleeting look.

clue.text: Telephone out of action is the limit

parts.note: a dead device is not working
a telephone line

explanation.surface: A phone that has stopped working is the last straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the time limit by which something must be done.

clue.text: Note kind of brush taken up by Impressionist

parts.note: D is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down answer taken up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sagebrush is a shrub of the American West

explanation.surface: A note about a type of paintbrush taken up by an Impressionist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' suggests paint, but sagebrush is a desert shrub; 'taken up' turns SAGE to EGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French painter of the Impressionist group, known for ballet dancers.

clue.text: Owing loyalty to a Belgian community

definitions.meaning: a feudal vassal bound to serve a lord
a city in eastern Belgium

explanation.surface: Being loyal to a town in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal term for bound in allegiance, and a city on the Meuse in Wallonia.

clue.text: State vehicle found in Italian resort

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An American state car turns up at a seaside town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside holiday town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Harvest pear damaged

indicators.note: damaged means the fruit's letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: The pear crop has been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in a crop.

clue.text: The good old days recollected in Donegal, for example,

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means the letters are gathered again in a new order

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone fondly remembers the good old days in Donegal, an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' rearranges DONEGAL plus EG. Donegal is a county in north-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A past era of ideal prosperity and happiness, the fabled best of times.

clue.text: Abundant ingredient of cream — plenty of it

indicators.note: an ingredient is a part within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: There is lots of cream in the recipe, plenty of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful, more than enough.

clue.text: Entertain doubts about assistant to police inquiry

definitions.meaning: to distrust or mistrust something
a person 'helping police with their inquiries' is the polite phrase for one they ...

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a helper in a police investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: British police reports say a person is 'helping police with their inquiries' when that person is under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means mistrust; as a noun it is a person thought guilty.

clue.text: Prepared to wait for doctor's charge

definitions.meaning: tolerant of delay, uncomplaining
a person in a doctor's care

explanation.surface: Someone willing to wait to pay the doctor's fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee, but here it is a person in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means tolerant of delay; as a noun it is one under medical care.
